about.title: For the cars. For the collectors.
about.bodyMarkdown:
Tim’s Diecast Garage is a proposed Arizona home for Hot Wheels and collector cars — from a familiar mainline casting to the piece that becomes the center of your display.

## A garage with room for your taste.

Japanese classics. American muscle. European icons. A Formula 1 grid. The collection brings different eras, scales and styles together, with enough detail to help you find your own lane.

You can compare a carded piece with a loose display example, explore a larger 1:43 model, or put together a shortlist around one marque. There is no single right way to collect.

## Look closer before you choose.

The intended store standard is clear photographs, identifiable models, honest condition descriptions and transparent pricing. A card crease matters to one collector; the shape of a casting matters to another. Both deserve enough information to decide.

## Made personal.

This demonstration is for Tim, who is based in Arizona. The proposed name, sample collection and USD prices help show how his own inventory could look here. The images come from the original project archive; they do not represent a verified stock list belonging to Tim.

Save a favorite, explore its photographs, then try the demonstration bag. No account or payment is needed.

## An independent collector store.

Hot Wheels and Mattel marks belong to their respective owners. This concept is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mattel. A GreenLight example is identified separately so the maker is always clear.

[Explore the garage ↗](/collections)

guide.title: Find your collecting lane.
guide.bodyMarkdown:
A great collection starts with curiosity. It can be a shelf of childhood favorites, one carefully chosen casting, or a miniature grid that tells a racing story.

## Start with a theme.

Choose a manufacturer, an era, a paint color or a particular body style. A theme makes a small collection feel considered and helps you decide which new release belongs in it.

## Understand the presentation.

**Carded** means the model is shown attached to its retail backing card and blister. **Loose** means it is displayed outside the retail package. A collector box or display case is included only if the listing expressly says so; a photograph of packaging alone should not settle that question.

## Compare scales thoughtfully.

The catalog includes 1:64 and larger 1:43 examples. Scale is a proportion, not a universal measurement in inches. For a tight display cabinet, ask for actual dimensions rather than relying on the scale label alone.

## Read condition as carefully as the model name.

For a carded car, inspect corners, creases, hanger tabs, blister clarity and any separation between the blister and card. For a loose car, look at paint, windows, wheels, axles and moving parts. Request current close-ups when a detail matters to you.

## Be precise about special editions.

Collector terminology is not interchangeable. A premium-looking finish does not, by itself, establish a Treasure Hunt, Super Treasure Hunt, chase or limited release. Compare the actual package, base and edition details before paying a rarity premium.

## Display and store with care.

Keep pieces dry, away from prolonged direct sunlight and excessive heat. Choose storage that protects card edges and does not press against delicate blisters. Keep original packaging and purchase records when they matter to your collection.

## Buy for enjoyment.

Set a budget, keep a shortlist and resist promises of guaranteed future value. This showroom’s example prices are merchandising illustrations, not appraisals or investment advice.

[Read the condition & authenticity policy ↗](/condition)

contact.title: Every good collection starts with a question.
contact.bodyMarkdown:
Need a closer look at a card edge, help identifying a scale, or clarity about what is included? Those are exactly the questions a collector store should make easy to ask.

Tim’s Arizona store is currently a demonstration. No support inbox, payment provider or order service is connected. We will show the verified contact channel here before accepting customer enquiries or orders.

## The proposed customer-care standard.

For the operating store, the proposed response target is within two business days, Monday through Friday, excluding US holidays. Tim must approve the service schedule and publish the actual support address. An automated acknowledgement would not replace a substantive response.

## What to include in an enquiry.

Use the product name and reference number from the item page. For an existing order, include the order reference and a short description of the issue. For a condition concern, supply clear photographs through the approved support channel. Never send card numbers, security codes or passwords.

## Frequently asked questions.

Can I buy these examples today?

No. This is a full browsing demonstration, with a sample bag and checkout review. It does not take money, create orders or reserve inventory.

Are these Tim’s actual cars?

The photographs are from the original website project. The 34 vehicle examples demonstrate how Tim’s own collection could be presented. Tim will replace or approve each sale listing, its current photos, condition and stock before launch.

What do the example prices mean?

They are illustrative US-dollar asking prices, chosen to demonstrate a varied catalog. They are not live valuations, certified appraisals or offers to sell. Shipping and tax are separate unless expressly stated.

Do you ship outside Arizona?

The proposed launch scope is the contiguous United States. The example shipping policy explains handling, tracking, packaging and delivery estimates; international service is not proposed for the initial launch.

Will the actual item match the photo?

The proposed store standard is to use current photographs of the actual item, or clearly identify representative photos. Any material packaging wear, missing part or difference should be disclosed before purchase. Archive photos in this demo are illustrative.

Can I return a collectible?

The proposed policy allows return requests within 14 calendar days of delivery, with condition and packaging requirements explained in the full policy. This is a suggested business term for Tim’s approval, not a return right created by this demo.

Do I need an account?

No. The showroom uses local browser storage for your shortlist and bag. No name, address or payment information is requested.

Can you guarantee authenticity or future value?

This demonstration offers no professional authentication, grading, manufacturer authorization or future-value guarantee. See the condition policy for the proposed approach to accurate product identification.

[Shipping information](/shipping) · [Returns & cancellations](/returns) · [Condition & authenticity](/condition)

privacy.title: Your information. Handled with care.
privacy.bodyMarkdown:
Current showroom notice · November 3, 2026. This section describes what the demonstration actually does. The future-store section below is a proposed plan and is not active.

## 1\. Who this notice concerns.

Tim’s Diecast Garage is the proposed name for Tim’s Arizona-based collector store. The final legal seller identity and privacy contact have not yet been established. This demonstration does not accept orders, contact messages, account registrations or newsletter signups.

## 2\. Information used in this demonstration.

The bag stores product identifiers, selected options and quantities. The shortlist stores favorite product identifiers. Both are saved in your browser on this device. When you verify a sample subtotal, the selected product identifiers, options and quantities are sent to the site server for calculation. The response is a sample quote, not an order.

The site and hosting infrastructure also receive technical connection information necessary to deliver and protect the service, including request paths, IP addresses, timestamps and browser headers. The website does not maintain a customer-profile database. Hosting and security logs may be maintained by the hosting provider; a business retention schedule must be confirmed before trading.

## 3\. Local storage and your choices.

Local selections remain until you remove them, clear site data or your browser clears them. They do not synchronize to another device. You can delete the bag and favorites now using the control below.

## 4\. Tracking, sharing and payments.

The showroom loads its fonts, images and film from the site itself. It does not use advertising pixels, third-party analytics, behavioral advertising or marketing cookies. It does not sell or share customer profiles for advertising. No payment provider is connected, and the site does not collect card information.

## 5\. Proposed privacy approach for a future store.

Before launch, the final notice should identify the responsible business and describe any order, support or account data collected. A typical order would require contact information, a shipping address and order details. The selected payment provider should process payment credentials through its protected service; the store should receive only the information needed to manage the transaction.

Sharing should be limited to necessary service providers such as the host, payment processor, delivery carrier and transactional-message provider, plus disclosures required by applicable law. Provider identities, processing locations, retention periods and any additional privacy rights must be assessed and documented before those services are enabled.

## 6\. Marketing, children and security.

No marketing consent is inferred from browsing or adding a product. The proposed store is designed for adult purchasers; children should not submit personal information or place orders without an appropriate adult. The operating store must use reasonable access, transport and data-handling safeguards, but should not promise absolute security.

## 7\. Requests and updates.

Use the local controls above for this preview. A verified privacy request channel will be published on [Customer care](/contact) before customer data collection begins. If the collection or use of information changes, this notice must be updated before the new use starts.

[Read the cookies & local storage notice ↗](/cookies)

## Administrator accounts and management data

Garage Admin stores the username, display name, role, password hash, recovery-code hash and recent management activity on the site’s persistent storage. It uses a secure, HTTP-only session cookie for signed-in administrators. Uploaded media, product drafts, page drafts and content snapshots are stored to operate and recover the site. Passwords and recovery codes are not stored in readable form. Owners can revoke access and download content backups. Team invitations are shared manually; no email is sent. This is separate from ordinary visitors’ device-local bags and shortlists.

terms.title: The details behind the garage.
terms.bodyMarkdown:
**Demonstration policy · November 3, 2026.** These are proposed operating terms for Tim’s Arizona-based store, shown so you can explore the complete customer experience. Orders and payments are closed. Tim must approve the final terms, business identity and support details before sales begin.

## 1\. Scope and seller.

These terms describe use of the Tim’s Diecast Garage demonstration and outline proposed terms for a future independent collector store based in Arizona, United States. The final business name, address where legally required and support contact must be published before trading.

## 2\. Demonstration catalog.

Catalog images, descriptions and prices demonstrate a possible assortment. A displayed example is not a verified statement of Tim’s stock, an appraisal, or an offer currently open for acceptance. Adding a piece to the bag or verifying the sample subtotal does not create an order or reserve inventory.

## 3\. Proposed order process.

For a future store, customers should be able to review item details, quantity, delivery costs, applicable tax and total before submitting payment. An order acknowledgement should explain whether an order has been accepted. Stock discrepancies, pricing errors or payment failures should be resolved before fulfillment, with clear communication and any required refund.

## 4\. Prices and payment.

All example prices are US dollars. The proposed store should show shipping and applicable taxes separately before payment and should never change the agreed total without customer approval. Payment methods, authorization, capture timing and cancellation handling must be disclosed after a provider is selected. There is no active payment method in this demo.

## 5\. Product description and condition.

The proposed store should identify the maker, casting or model, scale where known, package type, quantity included and material condition issues. Display props are not included unless the listing says so. Packaging photos and model photographs should not be used to imply a professional grade, rarity or provenance that has not been verified. See [Condition & authenticity](/condition).

## 6\. Shipping, returns and rights.

The proposed shipping and returns terms are set out on their linked pages. Delivery dates are estimates unless a specific guarantee is expressly offered. Nothing in these drafts is intended to remove rights that cannot lawfully be waived. The final store must comply with applicable consumer, delivery and refund requirements.

## 7\. Purchaser responsibilities.

For real orders, purchasers should provide accurate contact and delivery information and be legally able to enter the transaction. Do not misuse the site, attempt unauthorized access, interfere with another visitor, or submit harmful content. Collectibles with small parts are not suitable for every age; follow the maker’s product-specific age and safety warnings.

## 8\. Intellectual property and affiliation.

Hot Wheels, Mattel, vehicle marques, entertainment marks and related designs belong to their respective owners. Tim’s Diecast Garage is an independent proposed retailer and is not an official Mattel store. Site assets must be used only with appropriate permission. No license to copy product imagery or branding is granted by browsing.

## 9\. Value and availability.

Collectible prices can change. No future resale value, investment return, permanent availability, professional authentication or grading service is promised. A genuine defect or misdescription should be addressed through the published customer-care process, not dismissed as a market fluctuation.

## 10\. Updates and questions.

Material changes should apply prospectively and should not rewrite a completed order’s agreed terms. The final legal terms and dispute process require review for the actual operating business. See [Customer care](/contact) for the current contact status.

shipping.title: Packed for the journey. Ready for the shelf.
shipping.bodyMarkdown:
**Demonstration policy · November 3, 2026.** These are proposed operating terms for Tim’s Arizona-based store, shown so you can explore the complete customer experience. Orders and payments are closed. Tim must approve the final terms, business identity and support details before sales begin.

A collectible needs more than a label on a box. These example terms show a practical shipping approach for carded cars, loose models and larger display pieces.

## Proposed shipping at a glance.

| Item | Example operating term |
| --- | --- |
| Destination | Contiguous United States at launch |
| Handling | Dispatch within 2 business days after accepted, cleared payment |
| Standard delivery | Estimated 3–7 business days after carrier acceptance |
| Example rate | {{shipping_rate}} standard shipping; free at a {{free_shipping_threshold}} merchandise subtotal |
| Tracking | Tracking reference after the carrier handoff is recorded |
| International orders | Not included in the proposed initial launch |

Business days mean Monday through Friday, excluding US holidays. Handling and transit are separate. These are example service terms for Tim’s approval, not an active delivery guarantee.

## Protecting carded and loose pieces.

The proposed packing method uses a sturdy outer box and cushioning appropriate to the item. Carded pieces should be protected from bending and pressure on the blister; loose pieces should be secured so they cannot move freely against one another. A protector, display case or gift box is included only when the listing expressly says so.

## Address review and changes.

The buyer should review the full address before confirming an order. A change request should be made before dispatch and confirmed by support; a request alone does not prove the change is complete. Undeliverable or returned shipments require a case review before replacement or reshipment charges are agreed.

## Tracking and delays.

A label-created message is not the same as carrier acceptance. The operating store should explain dispatch status clearly and investigate stalled or missing tracking with the carrier. Weather, holidays and network disruptions can affect estimates. If the store cannot meet an agreed shipping promise, it should communicate the revised timing and the customer’s cancellation/refund options as required by applicable rules.

## Damage, missing pieces or a lost shipment.

Keep the outer box, packing material and item, and contact support with the order reference and clear photographs. The proposed process is to review the facts and arrange an appropriate replacement or refund where the store is responsible. Transit insurance and carrier claims should not be presented as a substitute for the store’s customer obligations.

## What the demo checkout calculates.

The bag uses the proposed {{shipping_rate}}/free-at-{{free_shipping_threshold}} rule as an example shipping calculation. Sales tax is not calculated, and no amount is payable. A live store must validate the destination, carrier options and tax treatment before charging.

[Returns & cancellations ↗](/returns)

Delivery-policy reference: [FTC guidance for internet-order merchandise](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/business-guide-ftcs-mail-internet-or-telephone-order-merchandise-rule). Final business terms require review before launch.

returns.title: Collect with confidence. Know the return terms.
returns.bodyMarkdown:
**Demonstration policy · November 3, 2026.** These are proposed operating terms for Tim’s Arizona-based store, shown so you can explore the complete customer experience. Orders and payments are closed. Tim must approve the final terms, business identity and support details before sales begin.

## The proposed return window.

For the operating store, the suggested policy is to accept return requests within **14 calendar days after delivery**. After a return is approved and instructions are supplied, the suggested dispatch window is a further 14 calendar days. Tim must approve these timeframes, the support process and a suitable return address before launch.

## Condition of a change-of-mind return.

A returned item should be the same item, complete and in the condition supplied, with included accessories and packaging. Opening a sealed blister, modifying a model, swapping parts or damaging a card can affect a collectible’s condition and the eligibility of a change-of-mind return. These limits should not be used to deny a valid claim for an incorrect, defective or materially misdescribed item.

## Start with customer care.

Request instructions before sending a return. Include the order reference, the item and the reason for the request. For damage or a description concern, include photographs where possible. Do not send a parcel to a personal address or to an address found in an old message without confirming the current return instructions.

## Who pays return shipping?

The suggested policy is for the buyer to pay reasonable tracked return postage for a change of mind. Where an incorrect, damaged or materially misdescribed item is the store’s responsibility, the store should provide an appropriate prepaid route or agree reimbursement. Costs and any exceptions should be explained before a return is sent.

## Inspection and refund timing.

The proposed target is to inspect a received return and initiate an approved refund within five business days. The payment provider may take additional time to post it. The operating store should use the original payment method where available, explain any lawful deduction with evidence, and state clearly whether original outbound shipping is refundable in the circumstances. No blanket restocking fee is proposed here.

## Cancelling before dispatch.

The proposed process allows a cancellation request before dispatch. Support should confirm whether the order can still be stopped and how any payment will be returned. If a parcel has already left, the returns process may apply. Do not assume a request has succeeded until it is confirmed.

## Incorrect, damaged or missing items.

Report problems promptly and keep packaging while the issue is reviewed. An appropriate remedy may be a replacement, refund or another solution agreed with the buyer. A short reporting target should not extinguish legal rights that continue to apply.

## Special cases and rights.

No custom-order, preorder, clearance or final-sale program is active in this demonstration. Any future exclusions must be disclosed before checkout and must respect applicable law. These example terms do not remove non-waivable consumer rights.

[Customer care ↗](/contact) · [Condition & authenticity ↗](/condition)

condition.title: The right details. No guesswork.
condition.bodyMarkdown:
**Demonstration policy · November 3, 2026.** These are proposed operating terms for Tim’s Arizona-based store, shown so you can explore the complete customer experience. Orders and payments are closed. Tim must approve the final terms, business identity and support details before sales begin.

For a collector, the card can matter as much as the car. The intended store standard is to describe both, show the relevant details, and avoid claims that the evidence cannot support.

## Condition language.

| Presentation | What a sale listing should explain |
| --- | --- |
| Carded / packaged | Whether the blister or seal appears intact, plus card creases, corner wear, yellowing, cracks, separation or other visible issues |
| Loose | Paint and decoration, windows, wheels, axles, moving parts and any missing component |
| Boxed / set | Exactly which vehicles, accessories, inserts and outer packaging are included |
| Modified / custom | Repaints, wheel swaps, opened bases, replacement parts or other known alterations |

## No unsupported grades.

Terms such as mint, professionally graded, certified authentic, factory error or limited edition should be used only when the evidence supports the specific claim. A sealed-looking package is not, by itself, proof of a professional condition grade or provenance. No third-party grading or authentication service is included in this demo.

## Photographs and identification.

The final store should show current images of the actual item wherever practical and label representative photographs clearly. Casting name, series, scale and packaging should be checked against the piece being offered. If a release year, variation or rarity cannot be established, that uncertainty should be stated rather than guessed.

## The examples you see now.

This showroom uses original-project archive photographs. Descriptions identify visible package labels and observable styling. They are demonstration listings, not certificates of authenticity or confirmed sale inventory. The GreenLight Cadillac is explicitly identified as a different maker.

## What if an item is wrong?

The proposed commitment is to review a credible misidentification, undisclosed modification or material condition mismatch fairly and offer an appropriate remedy where the store is responsible. This is a proposed customer-care standard for Tim’s approval, not a promise of professional appraisal or an unlimited authenticity guarantee.

## Safety and value.

Follow the actual manufacturer’s age and safety warnings. Collector products may contain small parts and are not automatically suitable for children. No resale value, investment return or future scarcity is guaranteed.

[Read the proposed returns process ↗](/returns)

cookies.title: A simpler kind of browsing.
cookies.bodyMarkdown:
No advertising pixels. No third-party video embed. No analytics consent inferred from your visit. This notice describes the storage used by the demonstration today.

## What is stored.

| Browser entry | Purpose and duration |
| --- | --- |
| velocity-bag-v2 | Product IDs, options and quantities in your bag; stays until removed or browser data is cleared |
| velocity-saved-v2 | Product IDs in your shortlist; stays until removed or browser data is cleared |

The internal names are retained from the original project so existing demo selections continue working. They do not contain a customer name, email, postal address, payment number or advertising identifier.

## Cookies and external services.

The showroom application does not set login, advertising or analytics cookies. Images, styling and the optional film are served by the same site. A normal external reference link opens the referenced provider only when you choose it; that provider has its own privacy practices.

## Control your selections.

Remove individual items in the bag or shortlist, use the button below, or clear this site’s data in your browser. If local storage is unavailable, selections may last only for the current visit.

## Future integrations.

Payment, account, support, analytics or marketing tools could change the storage required. Before adding them, the store must assess their purpose, update the notice and implement any required consent choices. Browsing the demo does not consent to future tracking.

[Full privacy notice ↗](/privacy)

## Administrator session cookie

The private management area sets a session cookie for authenticated administrators. In production it is named `__Host-garage`, is HTTP-only, secure and same-site restricted, and expires after eight hours. Signing out invalidates the server-side session. The public shopping bag does not require this cookie.

accessibility.title: More ways to enjoy the garage.
accessibility.bodyMarkdown:
The showroom is designed to support readable browsing, keyboard navigation and small-screen use. Accessibility is an ongoing responsibility, not a one-time badge.

## Browsing controls.

Use Tab to move through links and buttons, Enter or Space where appropriate to activate controls, and Escape to close the film dialog. A skip link leads to the main content. Search fields and filters have labels, product images have descriptions, and controls have visible focus states.

## Display and motion.

Layouts adapt to phone and desktop widths. Product photographs are contained so that important packaging details are not intentionally cropped away. The site respects a reduced-motion preference, and no film autoplays.

## Film alternative.

The original-project film is presented as an optional silent visual edit with native playback controls. It adds atmosphere; no product, price, shipping or policy information is available only in the film. Any future meaningful spoken media should include captions and a text alternative.

## Known limits.

Automated checks and manual visual reviews help identify issues but do not prove complete conformance for every assistive technology. Some archive photographs contain small printed packaging text; the item page supplies the principal model and scale details in readable HTML. Product-specific information should be available through customer care when the operating store opens.

## Feedback and assistance.

A verified support contact will be published before the store accepts orders or messages. The proposed support process should accept the page address, device or assistive technology used, and a description of the problem, without requiring sensitive medical information.

[Customer care ↗](/contact)
